title: How to Run a Customer Kickoff Meeting That Produces a Working Plan
summary: A customer kickoff should produce a shared working plan.
body_markdown:
A customer kickoff should produce a shared working plan. The meeting succeeds when both sides understand the desired outcome, the next milestone, the responsibilities, and the decisions still open.


A long product presentation can consume the session without resolving any of those questions. Prepare from the existing handoff so the customer can move forward rather than repeat the buying conversation.


## Prepare a short pre-read


Share the customer’s objective as you understand it, the proposed first milestone, the known dependencies, and the decisions the meeting should resolve. Ask the customer to correct the context and identify anyone else needed for those decisions.


Keep the pre-read short enough to use. Link to detailed requirements rather than placing every implementation document in the agenda. Separate confirmed facts from questions.


Review outstanding promises before the meeting. If your team owes setup instructions or a technical answer, acknowledge that obligation and its current owner. Do not wait for the customer to remind you during introductions.


## A practical agenda


Segment Purpose Output


Confirm the outcome Check the customer’s priority Agreed first-value statement


Confirm scope Identify included users and workflows Explicit boundaries and open questions


Map responsibilities Name customer and vendor owners Ownership for dependencies


Review readiness Identify access, inputs, and decisions needed Readiness checklist


Agree milestones Sequence the work realistically Shared plan with acceptance criteria


Set communication Decide where updates and escalations go Primary contact and update process


Recap decisions Confirm the next actions Owner, timing, and evidence for each action


Adjust the time allocated to each segment based on complexity. The agenda is a decision structure, not a universal meeting duration.


## Ask questions that change the plan


Ask what the customer needs to do first, who will perform the work, and what would make the initial result useful. Ask what internal approvals or competing priorities might affect the schedule.


Clarify who can make a decision when the working team encounters an exception. A sponsor’s name in the CRM does not necessarily mean that person can approve the specific implementation requirement.


Do not make the customer solve your internal organisation. They should know who coordinates the process on your side, even when several specialists contribute.


## Handle uncertainty openly


Some questions cannot be resolved in the kickoff. Record them with an owner and a review point. Avoid filling the gap with a confident estimate that later becomes an assumed promise.


If a requirement appears outside the agreed scope, describe it neutrally and route it through the appropriate decision process. Do not dismiss it casually or imply it is included before checking.


When the customer changes the desired outcome, assess what that means for the plan. It may require different prerequisites or a smaller first milestone. A useful kickoff adapts to the evidence instead of defending the original slide deck.


## Use a decision log


Record the question, decision, reason, owner, and supporting context. Keep open decisions separate from completed ones. This makes it easier for someone absent from the meeting to understand what happened.


For an illustrative example, the team may decide to begin with one department before adding another. The reason is that the second department’s requirements are not yet confirmed. The owner of that discovery is named, and the initial milestone remains focused on the first department.


The log prevents a later reader from interpreting the phased approach as an accidental omission. It also gives the team a place to record a revised decision if the customer’s needs change.


## Send a recap that can be acted on


The recap should include the agreed outcome, key decisions, actions, owners, and timing. Identify any unresolved issue that affects the next milestone. Invite corrections to the important facts.


Avoid a transcript-style summary. The customer does not need every conversational detail. They need to understand what was agreed and what happens next.


If AI prepares the recap, verify commitments against the conversation. An expression of interest should not become a purchase decision, and a target date should not become a guarantee. Our[meeting-action guide](https://o11.ai/blog/customer-meeting-action-items) covers this review.


## Follow through after the meeting


Create the work in the system the team actually uses. Confirm that owners have accepted it. Check whether the customer received the required materials and whether any dependency has changed.


The next review should begin from the plan, not from a blank agenda. Discuss progress and decisions rather than asking the customer again what they want to achieve.
